newsitem.title: FRANCE: DHL weighs new sites for Rhine Valley hub.
newsitem.headline: DHL weighs new sites for Rhine Valley hub.

text.p: DHL Worldwide Express said it had begun looking at other sites for its Rhine Valley hub after the publication of an impact study which called into question its project at Strasbourg-Entzheim airport.

DHL France chairman, Gilles Garin told Reuters: "While we have not officially withdrawn our Strasbourg project, one has to admit it is now unlikely it will ever be realised and our attention has now turned to possible alternatives."
The study recommended a postponement in DHL's project at Strasbourg until regulations were put in place which would protect the sleep of people living near the airport.
On Monday, the Strasbourg Chamber of Commerce, which manages the airport, asked DHL to withdraw the controversial project "in its current form".

Garin said: "It was regrettable that a minority of local residents, totalling 11,000, out of a Strasbourg conurbation of around 500,000 inhabitants, had determined the outcome of this project, which made very sound economic sense."
DHL chose Strasbourg from a list of candidates which included Nancy-Metz-Lorraine and a former military airfield at Belfort as well as unspecified airport sites in Germany.
"At this point in time, we can't say which sites we are looking or whether our choice will be made from the original candidates," Garin added.
The new hub would be set up to handle traffic in an area covering Nancy, Metz and Strasbourg in France, Basle in Switzerland and Stuttgart and Karlsruhe in Germany.
Major shareholders in DHL are Japan Air Lines Co Ltd and Deutsche Lufthansa AG.
